spatial_claims.claim: Ray AX is drawn from A, not collinear with AB, establishing a nonzero angle between AX and AB
Points P0=A, P1, ..., Pn lie on ray AX in order from A, with APi = CCi
Consecutive segments Pi-1Pi = Ci-1Ci by subtraction of equal initial segments
Triangle APnB is formed (non-degenerate since AX not collinear with AB)
Through each Pi (1 <= i < n), a line parallel to PnB meets side AB at Qi
Each Qi lies strictly between A and B on segment AB
In triangle APnB, line PiQi is parallel to side PnB and cuts sides APn and AB, so 6.2 applies giving APi:PiPn = AQi:QiB

configuration_map: Line AB is the uncut straight line. Ray AX extends from A at a nonzero angle to AB. Points P0=A, P1, ..., Pn are placed in order on ray AX with distances matching the divisions of CD. Triangle APnB is non-degenerate (A, Pn, B are non-collinear). Parallels to side PnB through each interior point Pi on side APn meet side AB at points Qi between A and B. The ordering of Qi on AB mirrors the ordering of Pi on APn. All subsequent reasoning is proportional algebra (Book 5) with no further spatial constructions.
pass_reason: All spatial claims are mutually consistent. The construction creates a valid non-degenerate triangle APnB, parallels through interior points of side APn correctly meet side AB at interior points, and Proposition 6.2 applies without conflict. The proof uses no angle decompositions, no interior-point arguments, and no betweenness-of-rays claims beyond straightforward ordering of points on a line segment. Steps 4-6 are purely proportional algebra from Book 5, introducing no new spatial assumptions.
